claude_code.verification_method: live run on 2026-09-23 against Claude Code 2.1.280, the version this row now records as validated_against — the first live advance on this row since 2.1.274. Evidence, all on the 2.1.280 build: `claude --version` reports 2.1.280; `claude plugin validate .` passes; `/skill-doctor` lists all 29 tamirs-superpowers skills with per-skill context costs; and `claude plugin eval . --case canary-can-write --ablation with-without` scores 1.00 in both arms, which exercises plugin load (suite.plugins resolves tamirs-superpowers), PreToolUse hook execution (enforce-worktree-edits fires and its degraded path is taken), and Skill-tool invocation end to end. The automated platform-sync job that opened PR #202 recorded this row as changelog-only because no live CLI existed in that environment; this branch had one. changelog + live-CLI method (automated nightly review). This entry had drifted: master's own copy stayed pinned at 2.1.263 (verified 2026-09-06/07) while the review work for 2.1.267 through 2.1.272 accumulated on this repo's long-open rolling `claude-code-update` PR without ever landing. The 2.1.263→2.1.273 reconciliation cycle (2026-09-16) merged that PR against current master and extended coverage to 2.1.273 on changelog evidence only, no live CLI being available then. The 2026-09-17 cycle had a live `claude` CLI in the automation environment, reporting exactly `2.1.274` — the current release at that time — so `validated_against` advanced all the way to it on real evidence, and `claude plugin validate .` was re-run for real and passed (marketplace manifest valid). 2.1.259–2.1.263 review (2026-09-06/07): `/skill-doctor`, `bashOutputMaxChars`/`taskOutputMaxChars`, a worktree-isolation permission fix, `/reload-plugins` for headless sessions — see CLAUDE.md's Subagents/Hooks bullets for the full per-item narrative. 2.1.267: the `effort:` frontmatter fix (directly relevant — 27 SKILL.md files here set `effort:`), `maxEffortLevel`, and a marketplace entry-path containment hardening protective of this plugin's `tamirs-marketplace` distribution. 2.1.268: `claude plugin install/uninstall/update/enable/disable --json` — adopted in `scripts/update.sh`/`scripts/uninstall.sh` (see `features_adopted`); `PermissionRequest` hooks firing in `--print` mode; `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS` fix; MCP `${VAR}`-placeholder secret-leak fix; agent-team untrusted-file isolation fix. 2.1.269 (largest delta in the range): a `PreToolUse` deny rule and the `Edit()` write-path check now also apply to a Bash `tee` write, and a `Bash(tee:*)` allow rule is correctly scoped — closes, host-side, exactly the gap `hooks/guard-sensitive-files.sh`'s header comment names and already covers independently via `hooks/lib/write-targets.py`'s own `tee` parsing (neither bug was ever exposed here, since `platforms/claude/settings.d/permissions-allow.json`/`permissions-ask.json` declare no `Bash(tee:*)` rule of either kind); a bare-`!` deny/ask rule leak is fixed (no rule here starts with `!`); the attribution-reminder-overriding-CLAUDE.md bug is fixed (this repo's CLAUDE.md asks *for* the trailer, so never conflicted); plugin-archive extraction hardening (host-side, no manifest change); `claude plugin eval` is genuinely relevant to this toolkit's 27 skills but its `case.yaml`/`prompt.md`+`graders` shape does not match this repo's existing per-skill `evals/evals.json`/`trigger-evals.json` trigger-accuracy harness, so it is tracked as a Future opportunity rather than adopted blind this cycle. 2.1.270: bug-fix-only (a same-week regression in 2.1.269) — read-only git commands in Bash no longer unexpectedly ask for permission after a long-running session; relevant since `permissions-allow.json` pre-allows several git commands specifically to avoid this class of friction. 2.1.271: a stale `.git/config.lock` after a sandboxed command failure no longer breaks `git checkout -b`/`git push -u`/`git config` for the rest of the session (Linux) — relevant since `permissions-allow.json` pre-allows `git push *`/`git remote add *`/`git init` for the same reason, and `hooks/worktree-create.sh` runs through the same sandboxed Bash surface; the Monitor watch deadline change (always at most 30 minutes, 10 in `-p` runs) — `skills/dev-workflow/pr-dev/references/ci-monitor-loop.md`'s one Monitor wrapper already sets `timeout_ms: 1800000` and never set `persistent`, so it was already inside the new ceiling; a background command no longer starting a second copy of itself after compaction, relevant to a long `orchestrate-dev`/`worker-dev` fan-out; cross-session `SendMessage` delivery now gives the headless sender a delivery notice instead of holding the message silently — documented in `docs/user/cross-platform-workflow.md`. `omitClaudeMd` (new agent frontmatter) and per-command `allowed_domains` for auto-mode sandboxing were reviewed and deliberately not adopted: no `agents/*.md` here should skip the target project's own CLAUDE.md, and no shipped rule runs Bash under auto mode with sandboxing. 2.1.272: bug-fixes-and-reliability-improvements only, per the official changelog; no adoptable item. 2.1.273: a 2.1.268 change that checked `Read`/`Edit` deny rules on Bash lines the permission checker cannot fully analyze (`eval`, `env -C`) is reverted — this repo declares no such rule pattern, so the revert changes generic host behavior but nothing this repo declares; `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1` now also tags cost/token metrics with real agent/skill/plugin/MCP-server names — not wired here, this repo ships no OpenTelemetry config of its own; the `New Features` section of the 2.1.273 changelog entry repeats 2.1.271's items verbatim (fast mode in Remote sessions, `/config` mouse support, `--drain-marker-file`, per-command `allowed_domains`, `omitClaudeMd`, `--accept-command <sha256>`, `modelPricing` multiplier) — already reviewed in the 2.1.271 pass above, no new review needed. 2.1.274: a sub-agent's progress summary is no longer replaced by a runaway multi-paragraph reply — directly relevant to `worker-dev`'s `completed`/`partial`/`failed`/`blocked` handoff vocabulary and any `orchestrate-dev` fan-out reading a worker's summary back; `claude agents` no longer loses `--model`/`--effort`/`--permission-mode`/`--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`/`--agent` after an auto-update — no script here shells out to `claude agents` directly, so not exercised, but relevant to a contributor invoking one of the ten `agents/*.md` from that CLI subcommand by hand; a visible low-memory warning is added (host UI, nothing to adopt); `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_STARTUP_WAIT_MS` is added — reviewed against this plugin's one MCP server (`github`, whose Docker fallback path can be slow to start on a cold pull) and documented as an available knob in CLAUDE.md's MCP bullet rather than set as a repo default, since the right value is workstation-dependent. Reviewed and found not applicable: an `effort` attribute on the OTel span (no OpenTelemetry config shipped here); Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/telemetry-disabled sessions defaulting to MCP client v2 (this repo targets direct Claude Code/Desktop sessions, not a Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry gateway); a sub-agent `model: "opus"` leaving the wrong session model on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry (all ten `agents/*.md` pin `model: sonnet`, and again no Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry usage); `/code-review` moving to leaner inline prompts (this repo references the official `code-review@claude-plugins-official` marketplace plugin in `platforms/claude/settings.d/plugins.json`, but has it deliberately disabled, so nothing here changes either way). Also reviewed for PR #154/#155/#156/#157 (2026-09-16, merged to master ahead of the prior reconciliation): SessionEnd-hook-budget fix, `handoff-reminder.sh` SessionEnd-schema fix, the 27-skill stale `model: claude-sonnet-4-6` pin fix, and the 3.6.3 release cut — all internal repo fixes with no platform-target, capability, or Claude-Code-host-version impact, so no co-change to the claims above was needed. Tonight's cycle (2026-09-20) had no live `claude` CLI in the automation environment, so this advance from 2.1.274 to 2.1.278 is changelog-only, covering 2.1.275, 2.1.276 and 2.1.277 individually plus 2.1.278: `reviewed_through` and `latest_known` move to 2.1.278 on that basis, same as the 2.1.263→2.1.273 reconciliation cycle did; `validated_against` stays at 2.1.274 — the last version an actual live `claude` CLI run confirmed — rather than being advanced on changelog evidence alone (an earlier draft of this entry made that claim; an automated PR review caught it and it was reverted before merge, see PR #159). 2.1.275: `/plugin install <plugin> --marketplace <source>` can install from a marketplace in one step; reviewed against `docs/user/install/claude-code.md`'s existing two-step `/plugin marketplace add` + `/plugin install` sequence and left as a Future opportunity rather than rewritten this cycle, since the two-step form still works and every existing doc reference assumes it. Skills and plugins enabled on a user's claude.ai account now sync into terminal sessions automatically, opt-out via `syncClaudeAiSkills: false`/`syncClaudeAiPlugins: false` settings — worth a `CLAUDE.md` note (added below) since a user who also has claude.ai skills enabled could see a name collide with one of this plugin's 27 `SKILL.md` names. Plugin/marketplace messages no longer leak a secret embedded in a URL, and `claude plugin marketplace update` no longer deletes the local marketplace copy on a failed fetch — directly relevant to this repo's own `/plugin marketplace update tamirs-marketplace` instruction in CLAUDE.md's Marketplace cache section, since a flaky fetch previously risked wiping the installed cache instead of leaving it untouched; documented there as a reliability improvement, not something requiring a manifest change. A send-now keybinding (ctrl+enter / ctrl+x ctrl+s) is an interactive-terminal convenience with nothing here to adopt. 2.1.276 carried no changelog entry relevant to this repo in the reviewed delta. 2.1.277: Claude Code now reads `AGENTS.md` instead of `CLAUDE.md` when a project has none, configurable under "Project instructions" in `/config` — this repo's own root always ships both (`CLAUDE.md` line 1 is `@AGENTS.md`) and `repo-scaffold`/`multi-agent-repo` always scaffold both files together for any new target repo too, so no project this toolkit touches or generates is ever missing a `CLAUDE.md` for the fallback to engage on; reviewed and recorded as not applicable, not silently skipped. The deprecated `TaskOutput` tool is removed (a breaking change upstream) — grepped every `agents/*.md` `tools:` line and every skill, hook and doc in this repo for `TaskOutput`: zero references, so nothing here ever depended on it. Reliability fixes to `Grep`/`Glob`/`Write`/`Edit`, plugin install/reload, and sandboxed Bash are host-side with nothing here to change. 2.1.278: Auto mode's server-side classifier now defaults on for API/Enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/gateway users (opt-out via `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0` on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/gateways) — reviewed and not applicable, same reasoning as every other Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/gateway item above: this repo targets direct Claude Code/Desktop sessions. No breaking change in the 2.1.275→2.1.278 range affects this repo (`TaskOutput`'s removal is breaking upstream but was never referenced here). Tonight's cycle (2026-09-22) again had no live `claude` CLI in the automation environment, so the advance from 2.1.278 to 2.1.280 is changelog-only; `reviewed_through`/`latest_known` move to 2.1.280, `validated_against` stays at 2.1.274 for the same reason it has stayed there since the 2.1.274 live run — nothing below is asserted as live-verified. The official changelog has no numbered 2.1.279 entry; 2.1.280 is the next release after 2.1.278. 2.1.280: directly relevant is the fix for skills being wrongly trashed on a `manifest.json` name collision (`~/.claude/skills/<name>` moved to `.trash/`) — this is exactly the collision class flagged as a risk in the 2.1.275 note above (a synced claude.ai skill sharing a name with one of this plugin's 29 `SKILL.md` names), so that risk is now a data-loss risk no longer, not merely a naming annoyance; documented in `CLAUDE.md`'s Marketplace cache section. Also relevant: `installed_plugins.json` no longer loses recorded commit info after a GitHub-repo plugin update — this plugin is installed exactly that way (a `https://github.com/...` marketplace source), so a user's install now keeps its recorded commit across updates where it previously could be dropped; no repo-side change needed, host-side fix only. `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH` is a new env var bounding how much of an MCP tool's description the host will read — reviewed against this plugin's one MCP server (`github`, via `scripts/github-mcp.sh`) and not set as a repo default for the same reason `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_STARTUP_WAIT_MS` (2.1.274) is not: the right value is workstation/model-dependent, not something the plugin can know in advance; documented as an available knob rather than a default. Claude Opus 5.5 becoming the default Opus model is reviewed and not applicable: every one of the ten `agents/*.md` here pins `model: sonnet` explicitly (see the 2.1.259/2.1.265 subagent-model notes above), so a change to which model `opus` resolves to changes nothing this plugin spawns. Reviewed and found not applicable or UI-only, with nothing to adopt: mouse support added to more fullscreen lists including `/skills` and `/plugin` skill-state options; hook output size stats added to the `hook_execution_complete` OTel event (this repo ships no OpenTelemetry config, same as every other OTel item in this history); the auto-mode retry-loop fix on safety-check denial/no-answer; the symlink write-path permission-judging fix; the disabled-skill indicator changing from a red ✘ to a dim ◯ (host UI only, this plugin declares no skill as disabled by default); multi-select option description indentation, `/skills` PgUp/PgDn wrap, and `/config` Tab silently changing a value — all three are terminal-UI bug fixes with no manifest, hook, or doc surface here to change; and the Code Review check-run REVIEW.md-cut notice improvement (this plugin references the official `code-review@claude-plugins-official` marketplace plugin in `platforms/claude/settings.d/plugins.json` but ships it deliberately disabled, per the 2.1.274 note above, so nothing here changes either way). No breaking change in the 2.1.278→2.1.280 range affects this repo. See `CLAUDE.md`'s Subagents, Hooks, MCP, Marketplace cache, Skill frontmatter, Claude Code CLI baseline and Remote and headless Claude sessions sections for the per-release narrative in prose form.

cursor.verification_method: live filesystem verification on 2026-09-23 of a real Cursor plugin install on macOS (Cursor 3.21.16 present on the machine). The materialized install at ~/.cursor/plugins/cache/tamirs-superpowers/tamirs-superpowers/<sha> is a full git clone of this repo at commit c9399aa (plugin 2.0.1, 2026-08-18), NOT a Markdown-filtered sync: `git status` inside it reports zero modified or deleted tracked files (only an untracked .cache-complete marker Cursor writes), and its 451 tracked paths diff IDENTICAL against `git ls-tree -r` of that commit. 263 of 452 files on disk are non-Markdown - 103 .sh of which 87 are executable, 14 .py, 53 .json - with hooks/hooks.json and all 25 hook scripts present; an all-files mode comparison against the source index found 0 exec-bit mismatches. Cursor keeps a second, equally complete materialization under plugins/marketplaces/. This answers #179's E0, which was BLOCKING on the fear that Cursor sync materializes only 'nested Markdown files' and would silently no-op the skills that depend on shell assets: it does not, and the structural reason is that the mechanism is a clone, not a file-type filter - the same conclusion the codex row reached by a different route. SCOPE, deliberately narrow: the install copy examined is plugin 2.0.1 and predates this measurement, and the invocation half of a Cursor validation (palette listing, invoking a skill by name) is still unverified, so validated_against stays 3.21.13 rather than advancing to the 3.21.16 binary on the machine. codex.verification_method: live run on 2026-09-23 against codex-cli 0.156.0 (installed via `npm i -g @openai/codex`) with plugin 4.4.0 — the version this change releases. First direct CLI validation on this row since 0.146.0, which it replaces. The repo was installed the way docs/user/install/codex.md documents, through a LOCAL marketplace so nothing published was involved: `codex plugin marketplace add .` resolved .agents/plugins/marketplace.json, and `codex plugin add tamirs-superpowers@tamirs-superpowers` reported 'installed, enabled 4.4.0'. An earlier attempt reported 4.3.2 because Codex reused a cached release; the cache was cleared and the run repeated so the evidence describes the released version. The install copy was inspected rather than assumed: 144 EXECUTABLE .sh files, hooks/hooks.json, 10 agent definitions and 35 SKILL.md all present, out of 4,670 files of which 4,274 are non-Markdown. A Codex install therefore preserves this plugin's shell assets and hook bundle, not only its Markdown — the same question #179's E0 raises as BLOCKING for Cursor and which no repo check covers, since the contract tests run against the local checkout and never an installed copy. `codex doctor` reports a healthy install. Both the plugin and the temporary local marketplace were removed afterwards. Release-delta review through 0.156.0 is recorded in docs/engineering/build-and-release/platform-targets.md.

Format verified against https://opencode.ai/docs/commands/ (flat .md under .opencode/commands/, frontmatter description/agent/model/subtask, body is a prompt template, $ARGUMENTS interpolation). NOT exercised against a live OpenCode binary in this pass - the generator, its drift check and the generated files are verified locally (26/26 parse as YAML; the drift check was confirmed to FAIL on a hand-edited command and on a stale command whose skill was deleted, not only to pass when in sync), but no live `opencode` run confirmed the commands appear in the TUI, so validated_against is unchanged. live run on 2026-09-23 against @opencode/cli 2.0.14 (`opencode2`), installed alongside the v1 binary which the package provides for exactly that. SCOPED — read what was and was not confirmed. CONFIRMED live: `opencode2 debug config` lists this repo's own opencode.json AND its .opencode/ directory among the resolved configuration sources, so the v2 flat-array `skills` form is accepted from a project config; and `opencode2 debug agents` loads 10 of 10 generated adapters from .opencode/agent/ (architecture-reviewer, debugging-specialist, implementer, integrator, orchestrator, performance-reviewer, research-agent, security-reviewer, spec-reviewer, test-engineer), each carrying this repo's own 'GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT / Generator: scripts/build-opencode-agents.sh' header, which proves the content loaded is ours and not a stale global copy. NOT CONFIRMED: per-skill discovery. v2 REMOVED the `debug skill` subcommand the v1 validation relied on — v2's debug surface is only `agents`, `config` and `paths` — so there is no CLI equivalent to enumerate discovered skills, and the /skill API route requires a running server. capability_source_note: targets.<key>.capabilities and capability_gaps are DERIVED from the capability registry and must not be hand-edited. Regenerate with `bash scripts/check-platform-targets.sh . --sync-capabilities`; `scripts/check-feature-equivalence.sh` fails when they drift.
version_claims_note: `validated_against` is the version this repo was last exercised against on a live maintainer machine. `reviewed_through` is the newest upstream release whose notes have actually been read for adapter impact. They are different claims and they drift apart on purpose: reading release notes is cheap and should always be current, while a live run needs a maintainer at a machine. V1-04 fires on `reviewed_through < latest_known` -- nobody has looked at what shipped -- because that is the gap a contributor can actually close. It deliberately does not fire on a validated_against lag, which is bounded instead by `last_reviewed` and V1-05's 90-day budget. A target with no `reviewed_through` falls back to `validated_against`, so consumer repos that have not adopted the field score exactly as before.
